ckd_staging.title: Chronic kidney disease: stage, hypertension and dialysis status
ckd_staging.question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's kidney disease and any related hypertension and dialysis status.

wrong_ckd_stage.description: Picked a different CKD stage than documented.

under_staged.description: Picked a lower or less specific stage than documented.

nonbillable_code.description: Reported a subcategory that needs more characters.

both_stage_and_esrd.description: Reported a CKD stage together with ESRD.

missed_htn_ckd_link.description: Coded hypertension and CKD separately instead of hypertensive CKD.

wrong_htn_ckd_code.description: Used the hypertensive CKD code for the wrong stage range.

diabetes_complications.title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
diabetes_complications.question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.

values.no: No statement that it is unrelated
values.yes: Provider says it is NOT caused by the diabetes

missed_with_link.description: Did not apply the 'with' convention, which presumes the link between diabetes and listed conditions.

linked_despite_provider.description: Linked a condition to diabetes after the provider documented it is unrelated.

missed_code_also.description: Left out the additional code the Tabular instructs (e.g., CKD stage).

redundant_manifestation.description: Added a separate code for a manifestation already captured by the combination code.

nonbillable_code.description: Reported a category/subcategory that needs more characters.

missed_complication.description: Coded diabetes without complications when a complication was documented.

coded_unsupported_complication.description: Coded a diabetic complication that was not documented.

missed_med_status.description: Left out the long-term drug use Z code.

only_one_med_code.description: Assigned only one Z code when both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used.

z794_for_type1.description: Assigned Z79.4 for type 1 diabetes, where insulin use is inherent.

coded_med_not_documented.description: Assigned a long-term drug use code that is not documented.

meat_support.title: Documentation support (MEAT) for chronic conditions
meat_support.question: Which chronic condition, if any, is supported for risk adjustment by this note? Choose 'no code' if none is supported.

values.med_list_only: A medication on the list only

missed_supported_condition.description: Did not code a chronic condition the provider monitored, evaluated, assessed or treated.

coded_without_meat.description: Coded a condition that only appears in a problem list or history without being addressed.

coded_from_med_list.description: Inferred and coded a diagnosis from a medication list.

unspecified_when_specified.description: Used an unspecified code when severity/type was documented.

scenarios.note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for hypertension and ESRD.

HPI: [Copied Forward] Patient is a 78-year-old male who presents for management of chronic kidney disease and hypertension. He reports being stable on his current medication regimen. He denies any new onset of peripheral edema, shortness of breath, or significant changes in appetite. He reports occasional acid reflux but notes it is well-controlled with current medications.

[Update] Today, the patient reports feeling well and denies any new symptoms since the last visit. He continues to experience minor symptoms of gastroesophageal reflux disease but states his current management is effective. He denies any acute changes in renal function or blood pressure fluctuations.

Vitals: BP 134/82, HR 76, Temp 98.6 F, SpO2 98% on room air, Weight 185 lbs.

Recent Labs: eGFR 12 mL/min/1.73m2. Potassium 4.8 mEq/L. Sodium 138 mEq/L. Creatinine 5.2 mg/dL.

Medication List:
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Atorvastatin 40mg daily
- Omeprazole 20mg daily

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, weight change.
Eyes: Negative for vision changes.
ENT: Negative for congestion, hearing loss.
Cardiovascular: Negative for palpitations, chest pain.
Respiratory: Negative for cough, dyspnea.
Gastrointestinal: Positive for occasional reflux. Negative for nausea, diarrhea.
Genitourinary: Negative for dysuria.
Musculoskeletal: Negative for joint pain.
Neurological: Negative for dizziness, numbness.

Social History: Retired. Lives with his wife. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol use.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had hyperlipidemia.

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3. Appears in no acute distress.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm. S1, S2 heard. No murmurs.
Respiratory: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, non-distended.
Extremities: No edema noted.

Assessment:
1. End stage renal disease: Patient remains stable on current management.
2. Hypertension: Well-controlled on current regimen.
3. Hyperlipidemia: Stable.
4. Gastroesophageal reflux disease: Stable.

Plan:
Continue current medications. Monitor eGFR and potassium levels every 3 months. Patient instructed to report any significant swelling or rapid weight gain.

Problem List:
- End stage renal disease
- Hypertension
- Hyperlipidemia
- Gastroesophageal reflux disease

Electronically signed, A. Rivera, PA-C, 05/12/2026

options.why: I12.9 is for stage 1-4 or unspecified CKD.
The classification presumes a link between hypertension and CKD.
Assign N18.6 only when ESRD is documented.

explanations: Hypertension with CKD stage 5 or ESRD: I12.0, plus N18.5/N18.6.
ESRD: N18.6. If a stage and ESRD are both documented, assign N18.6 only.

Follow-up for CKD.

HPI
Pt is a 77 y.o. female presenting for follow-up of chronic kidney disease. Pt reports feeling stable overall. Denies any acute changes in symptoms. She notes occasional mild heartburn, which she manages with lifestyle and meds. Reports no new edema, fatigue, or shortness of breath. Denies any recent falls or changes in mobility. Pt here for routine monitoring of stage 5 renal function.

Medication List
Omeprazole 20mg daily
Vitamin D supplement daily
Lisinopril 10mg daily

Review of Systems
Constitutional: Denies fever, chills, weight change.
CV: Denies chest pain, palpitations.
Resp: Denies SOB, cough.
GI: Reports occasional reflux. No nausea/vomiting.
MSK: Denies joint pain.
Neuro: Denies dizziness, numbness.

Social History
Retired. Lives with spouse. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol use.

Family History
Mother: CKD.
Father: Stroke.

Vitals
BP: 132/78
HR: 72 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on RA
Wt: 145 lbs

Recent Labs
eGFR: 12 mL/min/1.73m2
Creatinine: 5.8 mg/dL
Hemoglobin: 10.2 g/dL
Potassium: 4.8 mEq/L
Vitamin D: 22 ng/mL

Exam
General: Alert, oriented x3, in no acute distress.
Skin: Intact, no rashes.
Heart: RRR, regular S1/S2. No murmurs.
Lungs: CTAB.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no masses.
Extremities: No edema.
Neurological: NAD.

Assessment
1. Chronic kidney disease, stage 5. Stable on current regimen.
2. Gastroesophageal reflux disease. Stable.
3. Vitamin D deficiency.

Plan
1. CKD: Continue monitoring labs. Follow up in 3 months.
2. GERD: Continue Omeprazole.
3. Vitamin D: Continue supplementation.

Problem List
1. Chronic kidney disease, stage 5
2. Vitamin D deficiency
3. Gastroesophageal reflux disease

Electronically signed, D. Kowalski, NP, 05/14/2026

scenarios.note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for hypertension and chronic kidney disease.

HPI: The patient is a 77-year-old woman who presents today for a scheduled follow-up of her hypertension and chronic kidney disease. She reports feeling generally well today and denies any acute shortness of breath, chest pain, or significant fatigue. She notes that her joint pain from osteoarthritis of both knees remains stable and is manageable with her current regimen. She denies any recent changes in urinary frequency or significant edema in her lower extremities.

Medication List:
- Lisinopril 20mg daily
- Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5mg daily
- Naproxen 500mg as needed for joint pain
- Cholecalciferol 2000 IU daily

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, or weight changes.
Cardiovascular: Negative for palpitations or syncope.
Respiratory: Negative for cough or wheezing.
Musculoskeletal: Positive for chronic aching in both knees.
Genitourinary: Negative for dysuria or hematuria.

Social History: The patient lives at home with her spouse. She is retired and enjoys gardening and walking. She denies tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History: Mother had hypertension. Father had osteoarthritis.

Vitals:
BP: 132/84 mmHg
HR: 72 bpm
Temp: 98.6 F
RR: 16 breaths/min
SpO2: 98% on room air
Weight: 155 lbs

Recent Labs:
eGFR: 94 mL/min/1.73m2
Urinalysis: Positive for albumin.
Vitamin D level: 22 ng/mL (low).

Exam:
General: Alert and oriented x3, in no acute distress.
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, S1 and S2 heard. No murmurs.
Pulmonary: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Musculoskeletal: Mild swelling and decreased range of motion noted in both knees.
Extremities: No peripheral edema noted.

Assessment:
1. Hypertension: Well-controlled on current medication.
2. Chronic kidney disease, stage 1: Patient shows albumin in the urine; however, eGFR remains stable at 94.
3. Vitamin D deficiency: Confirmed by recent labs.
4. Osteoarthritis of both knees: Stable.

Plan:
Continue current antihypertensive and CKD management. Increase Vitamin D supplementation. Continue to monitor renal function and protein excretion. Follow up in 4 months.

Problem List:
- Hypertension
- Chronic kidney disease, stage 1
- Vitamin D deficiency
- Osteoarthritis of both knees

Electronically signed, J. Lindqvist, MD
May 14, 2026

options.why: The classification presumes a link between hypertension and CKD.
I12.0 is for stage 5 or ESRD only.
The note documents stage 1.

explanations: Hypertension with CKD is presumed linked: I12.9 for CKD stage 1-4 (sequenced first), plus the N18 stage code.
CKD stage 1: N18.1.

scenarios.note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for chronic kidney disease.

HPI
The patient is a 73-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up of his chronic kidney disease. He reports feeling generally stable but notes occasional fatigue and mild swelling in his lower extremities. He denies any acute shortness of breath, chest pain, or significant changes in urinary output. He continues to manage his symptoms with his current medication regimen and reports adherence to his prescribed treatment plan.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10mg daily
Sevelamer 800mg daily
Epoetin alfa 4000 units subcutaneous weekly
Vitamin D and Calcium carbonate supplement

Exam
The patient appears in no acute distress. Skin is intact with some dry texture. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Heart sounds are regular with no murmurs. Edema is noted in the bilateral ankles. Blood pressure is 138/84 mmHg. Heart rate is 72 bpm.

Assessment
1. End stage renal disease. Most recent laboratory work shows an eGFR of 12 mL/min/1.73m², confirming the progression of his chronic kidney disease.

Plan
1. Continue current medications as prescribed.
2. Monitor laboratory values every three months to track renal function.
3. Patient instructed to monitor for increased swelling or weight gain and call the office if symptoms worsen.

Electronically signed, H. Tanaka, PA-C, 05/14/2026
